summary: Verified Google OAuth 'double-verification removed' fix. Root cause of the user-reported 'Authentication Failed' was NOT only the double-verify — after removing it, the endpoint still crashed with HTTP 500 because the audit-log call in emergent_google_callback used wrong signature (`AuditLogger.log(db=db, ...)` with no `category`). Broad `except Exception -> 500 'Authentication failed'` masked the real error. Fixed in-scope (coding bug, aligned with pattern used elsewhere in the same file). After fix: 7/7 pytest cases pass, and the frontend Google button correctly chains: /login -> auth.emergentagent.com -> accounts.google.com.

minor.issue: Was returning HTTP 500 'Authentication failed' for every request. RCA: audit-log call used AuditLogger.log(db=db, ...) as a classmethod with missing required `category`. TypeError bubbled to broad `except Exception` handler. Fix applied: use `AuditLogger(db).log(action=..., category=AuditLogger.CATEGORY_AUTH, ...)` inside try/except (same pattern used ~20 other places in this file). This is what the user actually saw.

Broad `except Exception -> HTTP 500 'Authentication failed'` still present at line ~1935. This masks any downstream bug (as above) and any HTTPException with a specific 4xx. Consider narrowing or re-raising after logging.

action_items: Accept the in-scope fix in /app/backend/routes/auth_routes.py (emergent_google_callback audit log). No further code change is required to make the reported flow work.
(Recommended) Narrow the outer `except Exception -> 500 'Authentication failed'` block in emergent_google_callback so future coding bugs cannot silently masquerade as auth failures.
critical_code_review_comments: emergent_google_callback catches every Exception and remaps to a generic 500 'Authentication failed'. This exact pattern hid two distinct RCAs across the last two iterations (missing `logger` import in iter-35, wrong AuditLogger signature in iter-36). Convert to `except HTTPException: raise` + narrow `except Exception` that logs and re-raises as 500 only for genuinely unexpected paths — never for programmer errors inside the happy-path.
AuditLogger is instance-based (`AuditLogger(db).log(action, category, ...)`). Grep the codebase for any other `AuditLogger.log(` static-style calls to prevent regressions.
seed_data_creation: Created and deleted transient Google-OAuth users (email pattern test_gauth_*@example.com); cleanup runs inside the tests.

Covers: (a) success path posts valid emergent_user -> 200 with access_token and /auth/me verifies persistence; (b) same-email second call maps to same user id (update path); (c) 4xx on missing/empty emergent_user; (d) settings endpoint reachable; (e) normal login regression (success + invalid password). Frontend redirect chain manually verified: button click -> auth.emergentagent.com -> accounts.google.com/v3/signin/identifier with redirect_uri back to demobackend.emergentagent.com (Emergent-managed).
rca_of_the_issue: Developer's stated fix (remove double-verification) was necessary but not sufficient. After that removal, the callback still failed 100% of requests with `Emergent OAuth error: AuditLogger.log() got an unexpected keyword argument 'db'` (visible in /var/log/supervisor/backend.out.log). AuditLogger.log is an instance method (`self, action, category, ...`); the code invoked it as `AuditLogger.log(db=db, action=..., resource_type=..., ...)` which (a) passes `self` implicitly wrong, and (b) omits the required `category` parameter. The bare `except Exception` handler converted the TypeError into HTTP 500 'Authentication failed' — exactly the user-facing symptom. Fix: instantiate AuditLogger(db) and call .log(action=..., category=AuditLogger.CATEGORY_AUTH, ...) inside try/except, matching every other audit call in the same module.
